source.snippet: I am working on an application which handles some directory operations for a particular group of users. For this application, I need to create a least-privilege credential which can invite guest users, add these guest users to a specific AU, delete guest users, create groups inside the same AU, add guest users to the created groups. But as far as I can [tell], AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All is a tenant-wide permission with no way to scope it to a specific AU at the app credential level.

problem_statement: Enterprise developers building apps on Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) cannot create app-only credentials scoped to a specific Administrative Unit; the only available permission is tenant-wide, violating least-privilege principles and blocking compliant multi-tenant directory automation.
target_segment: Enterprise software developers and IT architects at mid-to-large companies building internal directory automation tools on Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD.
notes: Buyer context: enterprise IT teams paying for Azure/M365 subscriptions who need compliant automation. The gap is a Microsoft platform limitation — opportunity is in tooling, consulting, or a wrapper service that achieves functional scoping through compensating controls. Single ServerFault question with 0 score, so signal is weak; warrants monitoring for recurrence before heavy investment.
